items.text: Oil shock remains structural: WTI +10% and Brent +19% week-over-week (to Sept 15) reflect Middle East conflict and supply disruption fears. Energy-driven inflation is pushing core commodity costs higher, supporting PPI at 5.41% YoY. This inflation shock is unambiguously hawkish and favors near-term tightening, threatening refinance stress for levered corporates.

Sticky and broadening: CPI headline 3.35% YoY, PPI 5.41% YoY, and crucially, consumer inflation expectations spiking—University of Michigan one-year expectations jumped to 4.6% in September (vs 4.0% prior). Wage growth cooling (AHE 3.09% YoY) but not fast enough relative to price growth. Stagflationary dynamics emerging; credit investors should expect higher terminal rates and spread compression.

Fed tightening cycle resumed: Fed funds jumped to 4.0% (Sept 21) from 3.75%, extending the hike cycle. ECB followed with 250 bps deposit rate, citing energy shock and upside inflation risks. 10Y UST at 5.01%, 2Y at 4.76%, with yield curve flattening to just 20 bps (from 33 bps). Policy urgency is rising; long-end rates are near-equilibrium but front-end lift-off is creating refinance pain for floating-rate credit.

Spreads already re-pricing: HY OAS at 268 bps (tightened 8 bps) but IG OAS eased slightly to 77 bps (from 80). CCC OAS stable at 1083 bps—hidden fragility. Fed's aggressive stance and curve inversion stress are shifting capital away from duration risk into spread; special situations players should scan high-yield fallen angels and distressed refinancers.

Downshift signaling: GDPNow forecast at 5.08% (from 1.54% prior) shows volatile expectations; latest official GDP at just 1.5% (April print), well below trend. ISM Mfg at 54.6 in August (moderated from July 55.6) and new orders cooling to 53.7. Consumer sentiment collapsed to 47.8 in September, worst since start of crisis. Growth deceleration is becoming structural, limiting credit cycle upside.

Deteriorating demand signals: Existing home sales fell to 3.98M (Aug), mortgage rates jumped to 6.95%, housing starts declined to 1275K. University of Michigan sentiment at 47.8 (Sep) reflects income erosion and purchasing power collapse amid $4+/gal gas and broad inflation. Retail sales YoY at 6.93% masks the weakness; households are tapping savings (up to 3.0%), not building net purchasing power—watch for credit card defaults and HELOC stress.

Labor market softening: Initial jobless claims at 196K (down from 206K), unemployment stable at 4.1%, but payroll growth collapsed to just 162K (prev 21K—likely revision noise). Wage growth slowing (AHE 3.09% from 3.24%) while inflation accelerates—real wage compression will weigh on consumer. Loosening labor market provides cover for continued Fed tightening, but also raises recession tail risk for credit investors.

themeCards.title: Middle East Energy & Inflation Shock
themeCards.statusLine: US-Iran conflict driving oil to 107 WTI and 131 Brent, pushing gasoline $4+/gal. ECB just hiked to 250 bps deposit; Fed raised rates to 4.0%. Geopolitical tail risk remains unresolved.
themeCards.relevance: Energy-driven inflation and hawkish central banks are compressing credit spreads and forcing refinance risk into focus. Distressed energy-linked corporates and floating-rate borrowers face immediate stress. Special-situations investors should hunt for dislocations in energy supply chains and downstream hedging failures.

themeCards.title: Yield Curve Inversion & Refinance Cliff
themeCards.statusLine: 2Y-10Y curve collapsed to just 20 bps; 4% Fed funds with 5% long-end rates signals market-priced soft landing. But maturity wall looms: floating-rate debt, CLO refinance risk, and ARM mortgages all face higher rollover costs.
themeCards.relevance: The narrowing curve and front-end rate lift are stranding refinancers with mismatched tenors. Watch for cliff-maturity defaults, especially in mid-market and below-investment-grade space where hedges are light and covenants are tight. Special situations thrive in maturity-wall dislocations.

themeCards.title: Consumer Purchasing Power Collapse
themeCards.statusLine: University of Michigan sentiment crashed to 47.8 in September (from 55.2 in July). Gasoline at $4+/gal, inflation expectations at 4.6% YoY. Retail sales nominal growth masking real weakness; personal saving rising (3%) signals drawdown, not wealth.
themeCards.relevance: Real incomes are deteriorating fast. This threatens credit performance in credit cards, auto loans, and HELOC-backed retail credit. Specialty finance and captive lenders reliant on revolving credit growth face severe headwinds. Downside scenario for servicer valuations and ABS ratings deterioration.

themeCards.title: CCC & Distressed High-Yield Vulnerability
themeCards.statusLine: CCC OAS holding at 1083 bps despite broader tightening; speculative-grade issuers face dual headwinds: higher refinance costs (10Y at 5.0%+) and weaker consumer demand (sentiment at 47.8). Leverage multiples are stretched.
themeCards.relevance: Double-B and below borrowers in consumer-exposed and energy-linked sectors face the greatest stress. Rising cost of debt + falling demand = compression of EBITDA multiples and covenant cushions. Opportunities in CCC roll-up, distressed M&A, and broken-deal equity stakes.

themeCards.title: Housing Market Stress & Affordability Crisis
themeCards.statusLine: Mortgage rates at 6.95%, existing home sales down 2%, housing starts declining. Affordability indices near all-time lows. Refi market dead; purchase demand collapsing.
themeCards.relevance: Mortgage servicer cash flow is under pressure; MBS duration extension risk is real. Specialty servicing and non-QM loan dislocations creating opportunities. Builder inventory destocking will pressure construction finance; watchlist items for construction lender defaults and land deals.

themeCards.title: China Growth Slowdown & Supply-Chain Spillover
themeCards.statusLine: China official manufacturing PMI at 49.8 in August (below 50 = contraction). Stimulus uncertain; export weakness expected if global demand softens. US manufacturers already citing supply delays and cost inflation tied to tariff uncertainty.
themeCards.relevance: Global supply chains are under stress from geopolitics (Middle East) and China weakness, pushing input cost inflation higher (PPI at 5.41%). This inverts normal disinflationary tailwinds from offshore sourcing and threatens margin compression for USD-revenue corporates. Watch for breadth of supply-linked defaults among manufacturers and retailers.

retailSales.delta: August ex-autos strong nominal but masks real weakness

regime.label: Late-cycle transition
regime.detail: Energy shock driving hawkish policy, spreads firm but fragile; consumer collapsing on inflation expectations; growth slowing; refinance wall emerging
